Getting in

Four screens stand between a stranger and the record. Nothing here can be skipped.

Today

Thirty seconds a day, most days. It leads with what changed, because a number you have seen unchanged all week is not information.

Record

One record, several lenses. Every source writes into the same ordered stream.

Nadi

The reasoning layer. Claude reaches the record only through five typed tools, each already scoped to one person.

Care

Screenings, medications and the note you take to your doctor. All of it decided by rules, not by a model.

Profile

What only you know, and the controls over all of it.

Worth knowing

What these screenshots do and do not show

They are captured by an automated browser walking the real application — signing up, enrolling two-factor with a live code, loading the record, and visiting every screen. Nothing is drawn by hand and no state is faked.

Nadi's answers are the one thing missing. The build environment had no Anthropic API key, so the chat screen shows exactly what it shows without one: an honest notice, and the rest of the app working regardless. The same is true of document extraction, the morning read on Today and visit-prep drafting. Add a key and all four come to life — against your own record, which is a better demonstration than any screenshot.

The sample data is constructed, not copied from a real person, and it carries a deliberate story: fasting glucose drifting up over the last four days alongside three short nights, vitamin D stubbornly low despite supplementation, and a dilated eye exam that has quietly gone fourteen months overdue.
